_about: A recorded trip for the vacation simulator and the flow test: Boston to Lisbon, a party of three, one bad week. Links are to real sites; prices and ratings are illustrative. The live sources replace all of this the moment the API keys are set.

default.summary: Visit Lisboa. The official tourism site: neighbourhoods, events, the Lisboa Card.
Lisbon travel guide. Alfama, Belém, the trams, and where to eat.
Time Out Lisbon. What is on this week, restaurants, bars, and the Time Out Market.

flights.summary: TAP Air Portugal. Nonstop Boston (BOS) to Lisbon (LIS), evening departure, morning arrival.
Google Flights. BOS to LIS in early October from about $640 round trip, one stop via Newark or Dublin from $520.
Rome2rio. Boston to Lisbon: fly 6h 45m nonstop; no sensible rail alternative across an ocean.

hotels.summary: Booking.com Lisbon. Step-free rooms filter available; Baixa and Chiado are the flattest central districts.
Airbnb Lisbon. Apartments in Baixa with elevators from about $95 a night in October.
Pousadas de Portugal. The Pousada de Lisboa on Praça do Comércio, a splurge with a lift and a pool.

car rental.summary: Rentalcars Lisbon airport. Compact automatics from $38 a day; accessible vans on request.
Bolt operates across Lisbon; Uber too. Cheaper than a rental in a city where parking is a contact sport.
Carris. Trams and buses; the 28 is the famous one, the 15E to Belém is the useful one.

things to do.summary: Jerónimos Monastery. Manueline masterpiece in Belém; book ahead, queues by 10am.
Museu Nacional do Azulejo. Five centuries of tile in a former convent; Priya's whole personality.
Castelo de São Jorge. Views over everything; the climb is steep and the cobbles are unkind.
LX Factory. Old industrial site under the bridge, now bookshops, food, and a Sunday market.
Sintra and Pena Palace. A day trip by train from Rossio; go early, take the bus up.

restaurants.summary: Time Out: the best restaurants in Lisbon. Cervejaria Ramiro for shellfish, Taberna da Rua das Flores for petiscos, Ao 26 Vegan Food Project.
Belcanto (José Avillez) in Chiado; Prado for seasonal Portuguese; both reserve weeks ahead.
Michelin Guide Lisbon. Bib Gourmands under $40 a head include Zé da Mouraria and O Velho Eurico.

reviews.summary: Tripadvisor Lisbon. 4.6 average. Praise: light, food, friendliness, value. Complaints: hills, crowds at the tram 28, pickpockets on the 28.
r/travel Lisbon threads. 'Wear real shoes.' 'Skip the tram 28 at noon.' 'The Time Out Market is fine but go to a tasca.'

accessibility.summary: Accessible Lisbon. Step-free routes through Baixa and along the river; the Santa Justa lift and the funiculars are the shortcuts up.
Metro Lisboa accessibility. Most stations have lifts; Baixa-Chiado is deep but served; some Green line stations still lack them.
Sage Traveling. Alfama and the castle are the hard parts; Belém and Parque das Nações are flat and rewarding.

consulate.summary: U.S. Embassy Lisbon, Avenida das Forças Armadas. Emergency passports by appointment; lost-passport walk-ins weekday mornings.

destinations like.summary: Porto. Two and a half hours north by train; port wine, the Douro, tiles, and hills that make Lisbon look flat.
Seville. Moorish architecture, tapas culture, flat old town, October is finally cool enough.
The Azores. A two-hour hop; volcanic pools, no crowds, cheese, and the greenest place you have seen.

reddit.summary: r/portugal, this week: 'Anyone else stuck in Baixa during the march?' 'Peaceful, loud, avoid Rossio till evening.' 'Metro strike Thursday confirmed.'
Tripadvisor forum: 'Is Lisbon safe right now?' Replies: yes, avoid the demonstration route, taxis are fine.

default.summary: Lisbon tourism numbers hit a new October record; hotels near capacity.
Câmara de Lisboa extends the riverside pedestrian route to Belém.
Weather: an Atlantic front brings squalls Sunday, clearing by Tuesday.

protest.summary: Transport unions march on the Assembleia da República; Baixa and Rossio closed to traffic from noon.
Police estimate 30,000 at the demonstration; peaceful, one arrest, roads reopened by 9pm.
Metro and ferry workers announce a 24-hour strike for Thursday.

default.summary: Alfama rooftops from the Miradouro das Portas do Sol
Lisbon in 4 days: the honest guide. Trams, tascas, and how not to get pickpocketed.
We ate everything in Lisbon: pastel de nata, bifana, ginjinha, grilled sardines.

protest.summary: LIVE: Massive protest fills Lisbon's Rossio square, police lines on Rua Augusta.
Lisbon paralysed: metro strike, ferries stopped, tourists stranded at Cais do Sodré.
Is Lisbon SAFE right now?? What the news won't tell you (it is fine, mostly).

flights.note: Nonstop lands at 09:30 local, which saves a hotel night of jet lag. Trams and feet from there, as requested.

hotels.note: Baixa is flat, has lifts, and is where Dee will be happiest. Memmo Alfama has the view and forty steps.

cars.note: Do not rent a car for Lisbon itself. A car is for the Sintra day, and the train is better even then.

pointsOfInterest.description: Industrial ruin turned bookshop, brunch, and market; flat, photogenic, under the bridge.

pointsOfInterest.name: Alfama by tram and lift

pointsOfInterest.name: Sintra and Pena Palace
pointsOfInterest.description: Train from Rossio, bus up the hill, a palace painted by someone with no fear of colour.

pointsOfInterest.name: Time Out Market and Cais do Sodré
pointsOfInterest.description: Marco's pilgrimage; go at 11:30 before the crowd, then the riverside to Ribeira das Naus.

restaurants.name: Zé da Mouraria
restaurants.cuisine: grilled fish, plain rice, boiled greens

tips: 'Sou alérgico a marisco' (I am allergic to shellfish). Say it before the bread arrives; the bread comes with something.
Cataplana and arroz de marisco are shellfish by definition. Caldo verde and bacalhau à Brás are safe, as is most of the pastry.
For a recovering stomach: canja (chicken rice soup), grilled dourada, and no ginjinha for 48 hours.

mustEat.name: Cervejaria Ramiro
mustEat.cuisine: garlic prawns, the prego to finish

mustEat.name: A Ginjinha
mustEat.cuisine: sour-cherry liqueur in a shot glass by Rossio

praise: the light on the river at 6pm
the food, and the price of the food
how kind people are when you attempt Portuguese
complaints: tram 28 at noon is a sardine tin with pickpockets

transit: Metro: lifts at Baixa-Chiado, Terreiro do Paço, Cais do Sodré, Oriente; avoid the Green line north of Rossio.
Tram 15E to Belém is a modern low-floor tram; the 28 is a museum piece with steps.
Bolt and Uber vans on request; taxis rank at Rossio.
lodging: Baixa and Chiado hotels have lifts and flat approaches.
Alfama and Graça lodging is charming and unreachable with wheels.
attractions: Museu do Azulejo ground floor, Jerónimos nave, LX Factory, Parque das Nações riverside, the Santa Justa lift as a shortcut to Carmo.
warnings: Castelo de São Jorge: steep cobbles throughout, one step-free viewpoint.
Pena Palace: the bus stops below; the last 400 metres climb.
Cobbles are limestone and slick when wet, which on the storm day is everywhere.

ideas.name: Porto and the Douro
ideas.why: The tile and the food, with port wine and a river valley thrown in; the train from Lisbon is three hours.

ideas.name: Seville
ideas.why: Moorish architecture for Priya, tapas for Marco, and a flat old town for Dee.

ideas.name: The Azores
ideas.why: Volcanic pools and a rooftop of cloud; the pool day, but for a week.

plan.title: Seven Hills, Three Friends, One Pool
plan.plan:
The idea

Lisbon rewards a party that agrees to disagree. Marco eats, Priya looks up, Dee finds a rooftop, and every evening you meet at the river. Baixa is home: flat, lifted, ten minutes from everything.

The days

  • Sat 3 Land at 09:30, drop bags at Hotel da Baixa, first pastel de nata by 11. Easy afternoon; the Azulejo museum's ground floor and its cloister café.
  • Sun 4 Belém by the 15E: Jerónimos, the river walk, the original pastéis. Dinner at Taberna da Rua das Flores.
  • Mon 5 LX Factory brunch and books; Time Out Market for Marco's pilgrimage before the crowd.
  • Tue 6 Alfama the clever way: tram 28 up early, miradouros, Santa Justa lift down. Ramiro for the eaters, Ao 26 for Priya.
  • Wed 7 Sintra by train; Pena Palace; back for ginjinha at Rossio.
  • Thu 8 Dee's day: pool, rooftop, one gentle dinner at Prado.
  • Fri 9 Last nata, 12:40 flight.

A story

Fernando Pessoa drank his coffee at A Brasileira in Chiado every day for years, writing under seventy-odd names; the bronze Pessoa outside is the most photographed man in the city and the only one who never moved.
